route: data_labels / self-describing codes (code IS the source column header) + route 6 (keying polarity)
evidence: A: the live item code is the S2 Dataset (.s006) column header verbatim, 10/10 identical strings, and irw_table_sets("jablonska_2020_rses") returns exactly that set of 10 (no export used). Each header carries the items own abbreviated English wording ("30. I feel I dont have much reason to be proud."), so it ties itself to the S3 Appendix questionnaire sentence shipped for it ("I feel I do not have much to be proud of.") by content as well as by number 26-35; all 10 pairings were read individually and a swap of any two would be visible in the shipped English. B: keying polarity over the 974 complete cases of the S2 Dataset recoded 1-7 by the published LIKERT_MAP -- the five items whose shipped text is positively worded (26,28,29,32,35) intercorrelate +0.36 to +0.68, the five negatively worded (27,30,31,33,34) intercorrelate +0.33 to +0.67, and all 25 cross-block pairs are negative (-0.05 to -0.48); item means 5.12/5.46/5.31/5.34/5.04 for the positive block against 3.71/3.24/3.56/3.99/2.57 for the negative one. That is exactly canonical RSES keying (items 2,5,6,8,9 reverse) under the shipped assignment. NOT established by B alone: it separates the two polarity classes of five but not the order within either class -- that rests on A, which does distinguish every item from every other. B also says nothing about option_text, whose tie to resp comes from data/jablonska_2020_instagram.pys explicit label->integer map over the S2 Datasets own text values. Re-runnable as verify_jablonska_2020_rses.R (VERDICT: PASS).
